purpose: Next-token steering probes. Prompts are written to be OFF the target concept: they supply only an open syntactic slot, with no lexical or world-knowledge priming toward the feature. Any appearance of the concept in the continuation should therefore be attributable to the steering vector, not to the prompt.
design_principles: NO lexical priming: the prompt must not contain the target word, a synonym, or a collocate that pulls the target in on its own (e.g. 'set the ___' for 'tone', 'sheer ___' for large quantity, 'in City,' for a country).

NO world-knowledge priming: the prompt must not describe a situation that makes the concept the obvious completion (e.g. 'Penicillin was ___' for the accidental-discovery latent, 'They hadn't spoken in years when ___' for the suddenness latent).
NO contamination from the max-activating examples: no prompt reuses phrasing or subject matter from the dataset examples that defined the latent.
The slot must be syntactically available but semantically unexpected: the baseline continuation should be mundane and clearly different from the steered one.

Each latent has 8 'neutral_slot' probes (concept is grammatical but unmotivated) and 2 'override' probes (concept is not licensed at all; used to test whether a strong coefficient forces it in regardless of context).
revision_notes: 16167 rewritten completely: v1 named the city, so the country was already implied and the baseline model produced it unsteered. v2 contains no place names at all.

Contamination removed: v1 reused phrasing from the max-activating examples for 14298 ('Commander is a format of variety', chess search tree), 6879 ('flu jab... annoyance', 'Two names that appeared on the original patent'), 12380 ('Software does not just...'), 2043 (New Year gym crowd thinning in mid-February). These would have shown 'steering works' on prompts the feature was defined by.

Collocational giveaways removed: 'set the ___' (9050), 'broke it down into five ___' / 'in order, each ___' (854), 'there are ___' after 'so many' (14298), 'in order to' after 'changed the subject' (10081).
Explicit date anchors removed from 2043 and explicit 'once / used to / for decades' removed from 6879 — both were doing the feature's work for it.
Override probes added throughout so a null result on neutral slots can be distinguished from a weak vector.
usage_notes: Do NOT append a trailing space: Gemma tokens carry their own leading space (e.g. ' stages'), so a trailing space splits the target token.
Score by probability mass moved onto the target token set, and by short greedy continuations (5-15 tokens), not by argmax alone.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT for 16167: this feature fires on the country term inside an 'in City, COUNTRY,' apposition. Without naming a city there is no way for the country to be the immediate next token — so for this latent evaluate a 5-15 token continuation and check whether a location apposition appears at all, and whether it takes dateline form. Immediate-next-token scoring is not meaningful here unless you prime the city, which defeats the test.
Suggested control: run every prompt with an unrelated latent at the same coefficient, to confirm effects are direction-specific rather than a residual-norm artefact.
Suggested second control: run a coefficient sweep. Neutral_slot probes should show the concept before override probes do; if override probes flip first, the coefficient is in the degenerate regime.
